Confidence, odds intervals and full fight-level Kelly trajectories

October 19, 2026 · Follow-up to the full audit and statistical report · Code and saved analyses

Additional validation: see the earlier-data selection and Kelly robustness report for rules selected from past results, seven probability-estimation comparisons, allocations fixed at pre-card quote time, and uncertainty from 10,000 model refits. The fixed high-confidence filter remains promising; adaptive selection and stake sizing are much less stable.

Confidence 1, 2 and 3 separately: the lower-confidence and opposite-pick analysis adds confidence-specific intervals, NO-side pricing, search-adjusted uncertainty and interactive fight-by-fight Kelly paths. Opposing confidence-1 favorites is the clearest additional candidate.

Combining the strategies: the aggressive-growth comparison evaluates a single bankroll across discovered categories, settling each fight and reinvesting before the next bet. Individual Kelly stakes and model sensitivity are explained; simultaneous pre-card funding is a separate comparison.

Expanded sequential analysis: the 600-strategy Kelly comparison adds an interactive custom-fraction viewer, sizing learned only from earlier fights, later-period tests, and whole-card resampling sensitivities.

Per-fight stake caps: the 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% cap comparison measures ending wealth sacrificed and drawdown reduced, always sizing from the current settled bankroll.

Further confidence-2/3 research: the focused investigation and sequential viewer examines broader price rules, confidence-3 opposing picks, and whether earlier-data selection or calibration can recover their apparent edge.

How much signal is in confidence? The October 20 assessment separates the confidence scale's ranking information from the evidence for the discovered C2/C3 betting rules.

Yes—several confidence/price combinations have substantially higher historical ROI. The most useful new candidate is confidence 4–5 at 35–81¢: 32 wins in 43 fights, 29.5% net flat-stake ROI, and 47.6% quarter-Kelly bankroll growth with 11.4% maximum drawdown. These are exploratory historical results; the interval was selected after seeing the entire sample.

Practical interpretation: confidence 4–5 at 35¢ and above is a simpler candidate for future tracking than treating 81¢ as an established cutoff. It retains 25.4% flat-stake ROI across 49 fights and 43.4% quarter-Kelly bankroll growth. Neither rule has independent validation. Keep the 35–40¢ confidence 3–5 pocket as a separate hypothesis, and never stack two positions when overlapping rules select the same fight.

Category and Kelly optimization both use the full history; no category is statistically established after search adjustment.

What was tested

Every contiguous confidence interval and every distinct observed-price interval was examined: 52,156 backing combinations. All 15,292 positive-return combinations were simulated at quarter, half, and full Kelly using both initial-estimation conventions, producing 91,752 scenarios. There is no minimum-sample filter and no top-N exclusion. The maximum raw ROI is a single winning 16¢ bet (+490.3%); that is not a dependable category. The three-win confidence 1–2 pocket at 16–23¢ is also too small to treat its +374.4% as a repeatable expectation.

The viewer contains 111 candidates: the 58 ROI/sample-size frontier intervals, confidence-range leaders, Kelly return/drawdown frontier intervals, and broad references. Frontier means no alternative is better on both displayed dimensions. It is a descriptive comparison, not an adjustment for overfitting. All other positive combinations remain in the complete results file.

Whole-trajectory viewer

Start at bankroll 1 and advance after every source row in chronological fight order. All 187 rows are represented: 185 decisive fights, one draw and one canceled fight. Zero-stake rows remain flat. The draw uses a 50¢ contract payout if a position is selected. Forecasts use only earlier decisive outcomes.

Quarter KellyHalf KellyFull Kelly

Whole-trajectory Kelly requires an estimated win probability. It does not assume the eventual category win rate was known at the beginning. The Firth logistic model uses market log odds and confidence, refitted after each decisive fight. It first has full column rank after three observations; before that, stakes are zero. Every bet uses fraction × max(0, (estimated probability − all-in cost)/(1 − all-in cost)) of the then-current bankroll. Price reconstruction still uses the full paired-price dataset and pre-card quotes are assumed obtainable later; these are not verified historical fills.

The broad confidence-4–5 quarter-Kelly result changes from +10.2% with the earlier 24-fight training prefix to −7.2% when estimation starts as soon as the three-parameter model is identifiable. The extra early losing bet risks 15.8% of bankroll even at quarter Kelly because the sparse fitted model assigns a large edge. Full Kelly on the broad pool loses 68.3% in this version. This is evidence of estimation risk; selecting the longer warm-up because it produces a better backtest would be another hindsight decision. The 35¢-and-above candidates exclude that fight, but their threshold is itself discovered retrospectively.

A zero observed drawdown for a tiny winning subset is not evidence of zero future risk. The 35–40¢ pocket places only five positive-estimated-edge Kelly bets out of its eight qualifying flat-stake wins. No user risk tolerance has been supplied, so the report compares stake fractions rather than declaring one optimal.

Reliability of the new candidates

For confidence 4–5 at 35–81¢, the nominal card-cluster 95% ROI interval is 5.0% to 53.9%. The common-shift posterior gives 97.9% probability of positive expected ROI. Both are conditional, unadjusted summaries after category discovery. The search-adjusted flat-stake p-value is 1.000 after accounting for both directions.

Removing its largest winner leaves 26.0% ROI; omitting any one card leaves at least 23.5%. The 13 fights with observed Kalshi asks return 24.6%. After adding the empirical adverse reconstruction error to estimated prices and reselecting the interval, 42 fights remain with 22.1% ROI. For the simpler 35¢-and-above rule, the corresponding stressed ROI is 18.6% across 50 fights.

These checks make the filtered candidates worth tracking, but they reuse the same outcomes. Actual signal timestamps, complete pick coverage, available depth, fees at order size, individual fight start times, and settlement availability remain unverified. The main report’s frozen-before-card sensitivity illustrates why the positive sequential paths cannot establish executable historical profits.

Saved work

The complete positive-interval simulation summaries, selected-category statistics, displayed bankroll trajectories, ROI/sample-size frontier, and price-error sensitivity are saved alongside the code. Complete trajectories for every positive interval are saved locally as compressed arrays under artifacts/private/all_positive_interval_paths_prefix_*.npz. They can be regenerated from the supplied workbook.
